label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 5
knowledgePattern: Check the prime-divisor exception inside a contradiction proof
solution:
Lines I–VI are justified. If n is not a multiple of 3, its remainder is 1 or 2, so its square has remainder 1 and n2+2 is a positive multiple of 3.

Line VII is the first error: a positive multiple of a prime is composite only if it is larger than that prime. Here n=1 gives n2+2=3, which is prime, despite n not being a multiple of 3.

Thus the claimed contradiction need not occur. The first error is in VII, option H.

hints.title: Use the exact definition of composite
hints.body: Compare being a positive multiple of a prime with being composite. Check whether the smallest permitted inputs leave a special case.
hints.recap: Primality is defined by the positive divisors of the number; a divisibility statement must be checked against that definition.
hints.pitfall: A general-looking algebraic multiple may include a small exceptional value.
